name: Tobiah
summary: Tobiah the Ammonite official, Sanballat's ally, who mocked the new wall: if a fox climbed on it, it would break down. He was bound by marriage to leading families of Judah, who kept up a stream of letters with him, and joined in hiring a prophet to frighten Nehemiah. While Nehemiah was away, the priest Eliashib, a relative, gave him a room in the temple courts; Nehemiah threw all his household goods out.
body: His son Jehohanan married the daughter of Meshullam, one of the wall's builders; he himself was son-in-law to Shecaniah. Nehemiah prays that God will remember what he and Sanballat have done.

moments.text: “If even a fox were to climb up”

later.text: Many historians connect him with the Tobiads, a powerful family east of the Jordan: a Tobias appears in the Zenon papyri of 259 BC, the name Tobiah is cut in the rock at ʿIraq al-Amir, and Josephus tells of the family's feuds.
